newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee recovers by close, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee recovers by close, more gains seen.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures ended Tuesday with pared gains after an erratic session and traders said the market was poised for a further recovery after a massive sell-off over the last few days.
"It is a reasonable close. Now with the shake-out, the market is vulnerable to a rise," said one trader.
Still, Brazilian weather remains a key issue for coffee.
Weathermen said a cold airmass expected over Brazil's coffee belt this coming weekend did not appear to be cold enough to cause damage to crops but this could change and bears a close watch.
London's benchmark July contract rebounded from early sharp losses on fund and speculative selling to post a hefty $170 gain at one stage as the market tracked a steep rise in New York.
By the close, it stood at $2,150 per tonne, a $40 rise on the day after fluctuating by $254.

The contract however failed to completely fill a chart gap between $2,262 and $2,360 on the upside, left after last week's rally to a 20-month-high of $2,670. The gap is now seen as an immediate technical barrier.
On the downside, support is seen at $2,000 followed by a chart gap from $1,940 to $1,973.

Earlier in the session, a fresh wave of spec profit-taking took benchmark July to a session low of $2,026, hitting a few sell-stops as the market fell below Monday's low of $2,100 and last week's double-bottom of $2,065.
Traders said the selling was well absorbed by buyers who had gone short last week.
New York's July rose to a high of 268.50 cents a lb, but still below last week's peak of over 300.00 cents.
Traders said with the steep exchange margins in New York, any large buying or selling orders move the market.
"This was what happened today," said one. "People are watching the volume they trade. A reasonable volume could move the market."
Overall volume in London reached 10,113 lots. The active July/Sept switch stood at $40 by the close, up from $15 on Monday.
